Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

evidence noun

in a court: testimony

also testimony, give evidence, testify, bear witness, witness statement, admissible, not admissible, turn state’s evidence, give evidence against

classical

Cic. Brut. 293: quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus
Ter. Ph. 293: neque testimōnī dictiō est
Traupman 195, 311

testimōnium, testimōniī n.

noun, second declension

evidence, testimony (of a witness)

To give evidence: testimōnium dīcere (Cic.); against someone, testimōnium dīcere in aliquem (Traupman 195, 311). A witness is testis; to bear witness, testificārī, frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • indicium, indiciī n. — information laid, an informer’s evidence

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Sall. Jug. 35.6: indicium profitētur (M-O s.v. turn state’s evidence); Traupman 195

    Indicium profitērī, to turn informer (Traupman 195; M-O).

  • indicium profitērī — turn state’s evidence, give evidence against one’s accomplices

    also used · classical · Sall. J. 35.6: multīs hortantibus indicium profitētur (Lewis & Short s.v. indicium); Traupman 311

Examples

  • vidē nē religiō nōbīs tam adhibenda sit quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus

    take care: we may need to be as scrupulous as if we were giving evidenceCic. Brut. 293

  • tum quī testimōnium dīceret ut arbitrārī sē dīceret etiam quod ipse vīdisset

    and that a witness should say “I think” even of what he had seen himselfCic. Ac. 2.146

  • Hoc testimōnium nōn sūmendum est.

    This evidence is not admissible.Traupman 195

  • testimōnium dīcere in aliquem

    to give evidence against someoneTraupman 311

  • Quō mē teste convincēs?

    On what evidence will you convict me?Cic. Phil. 2.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. convincō)

See also evidence, prove, charge.
